transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts at work, like I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout or sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I check and it seems fine, my mind keeps going back to it, and it’s been bothering me.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to get rid of these nagging thoughts?

Yes. Before I submit work, I’ll usually open the file again, compare the layers, re-save it, and then kind of mentally go through each design choice one more time. It doesn’t take over my whole day, but it definitely slows me down and makes me feel less free creatively.
Do you experience these nagging thoughts or feelings of needing to check things over and over in other areas of your life, outside of work?

I’m not really sure. I notice it mostly with my work, because that’s where the checking comes up. Outside of that, I haven’t really paid attention to it, or it doesn’t stand out to me in the same way.
Do you feel like these nagging thoughts and the need to check your work are affecting your overall well-being or causing you a lot of distress?

It’s not ruining everything, but yes, it is starting to affect me. I’m still getting my work done, but I’ve missed some internal deadlines because I keep checking things. And I’ve noticed I’m holding back on some bolder design ideas because I’m worried I’ll miss something and it’ll hurt my chances of moving toward a creative director role.
Have these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors affected your relationships with friends or family in any way?

I haven’t really noticed it affecting my relationships much. I mean, maybe I’m a little distracted after work sometimes, but I don’t think my friends or family have really been impacted in a clear way.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge when you're not working or thinking about work?
Not really sure. I mean, I can feel a little tense sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being a regular thing when I’m away from work or not thinking about it.
Do you feel anxious when you are completely relaxed and not thinking about work?

I don’t think so. If I’m actually relaxed and not thinking about work, I don’t really notice anxiety. It’s more that I’m not always sure when I’m fully switched off, but I wouldn’t say I feel anxious in those moments.
Do you often feel anxious when you are in social situations or interacting with others outside of work?
Not really. I mean, I can get a little self-conscious like anyone, but I haven’t noticed feeling anxious just because I’m around people or talking with friends outside of work.
Do you have recurring thoughts or ideas that aren't about work and feel intrusive or hard to control?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of recurring thoughts like that that aren’t related to work. Nothing that feels intrusive or out of my control comes to mind.
Do you have thoughts that aren't about work and feel like they're repeating over and over in your mind?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed non-work thoughts looping like that in my mind.
Do you often feel anxious for no specific reason when you're going about your daily activities?
Not really. I don’t usually feel anxious out of nowhere during the day. If I’m anxious, there’s usually some clear reason for it.
Do you have thoughts that aren't about work and feel like they're unwanted or hard to get rid of?
No, I don’t think I have that. I haven’t noticed unwanted thoughts outside of work that stick around or that I can’t get rid of.
Do you feel anxious about things in general, not just related to your work?
Not really in general, no. I mean, I get worried if there’s an actual reason, but I don’t feel anxious about everything or just day-to-day things for no clear reason.
Do you feel like your nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy your free time or maintain your relationships?

It’s not so much my relationships or free time, I guess. The main place I notice it is at work. I’m still getting things done, but I’ve started missing internal deadlines, and I hold back on some of my bolder design ideas because I’m worried I’ll miss something important. I’m afraid that could hurt my chances of moving toward a creative director role.
Do you worry about a wide range of things in your life, not just your work?
No, I wouldn’t say it’s a wide range of things. I’m not usually worrying about my whole life or lots of different areas. It’s more specific when it happens.
Do you feel anxious when there's no particular reason or situation causing you to feel that way?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed anxiety just coming out of nowhere. It usually seems tied to something specific.
Do you feel anxious about things outside of work, such as your health, finances, or personal relationships?

Not really. I mean, I have normal concerns here and there, but I haven’t noticed being especially anxious about my health, money, or relationships. It doesn’t feel like that’s where the anxiety is coming from.
Do you feel anxious in situations where there's no obvious reason for you to be anxious?
No, I don’t think so. I can usually point to something specific if I’m anxious. It doesn’t really happen for no clear reason.
Are your nagging thoughts and checking behaviors affecting your overall quality of life outside of your job?

Mostly it’s affecting work more than the rest of my life. I’m still getting things done, but I’ve started missing some internal deadlines. And I notice I hold back on bigger, bolder design ideas because I’m worried I’ll miss something important and hurt my chances of moving toward a creative director role.
Are you feeling like these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are significantly affecting your overall happiness or life satisfaction?

It’s not ruining my overall happiness, no. But it is frustrating. I’m still doing my work, but missing internal deadlines and holding back on bigger design ideas makes me feel like I’m not moving forward the way I want to, especially toward a creative director role. So it affects my satisfaction, mostly around work.
